steps.what: Read the open work order before recording anything
Record production, repair and machine maintenance information as stated fields
Copy the stated production, repair and maintenance into the record
Check the record keeps her production count, repair and maintenance
Write the accepted record into the maintenance history

tasks.design: She states the production count, the repair and the maintenance against the open work order. A copy fills those fields in the {OTHER} maintenance record and does not wait. She checks that the count, the repair and the maintenance are hers, and only the accepted record is written. A rejection writes nothing. She does not type the record as well.
tasks.previous_blocker: The maintenance record was a paper order or a second typing after the job, so the history and the work sat apart.
tasks.enabler_now: A work-order screen can hold fault, parts and times, and a short copy can fill those fields from what she states. Model knowledge.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to know what was produced, repaired and maintained. A wrong fault sends the planner the wrong job.
tasks.human_edge: She was at the machine. The record is only as true as what she states.
tasks.altitude: Stating what was produced, repaired and maintained stays in her week. Only typing the accepted record leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Keep the fault and cause list the work order closes against
reach.learn: Which codes the planner accepts, and which unmatched notes she must leave for him

evidence.claim: A maintenance-record product keeps preventive plans and repair history.
One fibre-network case reports about 8 hours a technician a week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports, and states no period.
Work orders that store time stamps or location can observe technicians, so works-council consent comes first.

assumptions: The machine id and the open work order already exist. She does not open the order in this task.
Blank production, repair or maintenance fields mean no copy.
Try the maintenance record's own close screen before custom code. Existing screen time is not her effort.
The copy does not rephrase and does not wait for the check.
She does not also type the record. The check compares the production count, the repair and the maintenance with what she stated. Any change voids acceptance.
Rejection writes nothing. The write is the close she already does today. A spoken handover with nothing stated is not a write.
Start and stop times are fields she states. The record stores no location.
The planner owns the fault list, so her added upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether this plant's work order already has fault, parts and time fields, and whether storing those times needs works-council consent.
research_questions: Does closing the work order today already capture fault, parts and start and stop, or is that still a paper note?

already_counted.description: The check that the record keeps her production count, repair and maintenance, already counted in the review step before the write.

incremental.description: A rejected record is dropped in the check. The planner owns the fault list, so her upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most jobs are a spoken handover with blank production, repair or maintenance fields, so the copy does not run. High: most jobs already close on a work order with those fields stated, and only the typing leaves. She still states what happened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate to repair or move machines.

steps.what: Read the machine and the parts named for this job
Collaborate with other workers to repair or move machines, parts or equipment
Decide how the crew lifts or turns that equipment

tasks.design: She still repairs or moves the machine with the other workers, and she still decides the lift. No message is copied and nothing is sent. The week keeps the whole job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Moving or repairing a machine with other workers is a shared physical act, and no screen can take a side of the lift.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the crew. Naming who is asked is already done by talking on the floor.
tasks.still_hard: The lift, the fit and the other person's hands stay on the floor.
tasks.human_edge: She feels the weight and sees the other worker. That does not move into a record.
tasks.altitude: The repair and the move stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Set the lift plan for a machine move
reach.learn: When a move needs a rigger or a permit rather than the crew alone

evidence.claim: Repairing or moving a machine with other workers is physical coordination on the floor. Model knowledge: no record takes a side of the lift.

assumptions: The other workers are inside the plant. A talk with them is not a send outside the organisation.
No written message already leaves with this task, so nothing is copied.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often a move needs a rigger or a permit the crew cannot grant.
research_questions: Which machine moves already have a written lift plan, and which are agreed on the floor?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The crew still lifts and repairs the machine together. There is no message that already leaves the plant, so no step shortens.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read work orders and choose the machine.

steps.what: Read work orders and specifications before choosing a machine
Determine the machines and equipment requiring repair or maintenance
Decide which of those repairs she starts first

tasks.design: She still reads the work order and the specification, and she still decides which machines need repair or maintenance. No summary is written for her, and no model chooses the machine.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order and the specification say what is wrong only after someone reads them against the machine.
tasks.enabler_now: The order can sit on a screen. Reading it and choosing the machine are still her work.
tasks.still_hard: A short order hides a long specification. She has to judge which machine actually needs her.
tasks.human_edge: She matches the written fault to the machine in front of her.
tasks.altitude: Reading the order and choosing the machine stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.learn: How priority on the order should change what she reads first

evidence.claim: Choosing which machine needs repair from a work order is the worker's judgement. Model knowledge: a generated reading would still need her at the machine.

assumptions: The work order and the specification already exist. She does not write them in this task.
No model reads the specification for her.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often the specification is a long drawing rather than a short fault line.
research_questions: How often the written fault and the machine in front of her disagree?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still reads the order and the specification and still chooses the machine. Opening the order on a screen does not shorten that reading.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect parts and advise the supervisor.

steps.what: Look at the damaged machine before any closer look
Inspect damaged machine parts and mark defective areas
Advise supervisors of the repair needs found on the part

tasks.design: She still inspects and tests the part, marks the defective area, and advises the supervisor in person. No recording and no written notice are added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Damage shows on the part, and a mark or a word to the supervisor is how the shop hears it.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in a record replaces the inspection or the test.
tasks.still_hard: A hairline crack and a dirty mark look alike until she tests the part.
tasks.human_edge: She sees and tests the part. The supervisor hears her, not a generated note.
tasks.altitude: The inspection, the mark and the advice to the supervisor stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Decide whether a marked defect stops the machine
reach.learn: Which defects the supervisor wants told at once

evidence.claim: Marking a defective area and advising a supervisor come from inspecting the part in person. Model knowledge: that look does not move to a generated note.

assumptions: The supervisor is inside the plant. Advice spoken to that supervisor is not a send outside the organisation.
No written notice already goes out with this task, so nothing is copied.
There is no recording of the inspection.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often the advice is a written note rather than a word on the floor.
research_questions: How often a marked defect is also written down the same day, and how often it is only spoken?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still inspects and tests the part, marks the defect, and tells the supervisor. A written notice is not added on top of that talk.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The lift, the reading of the order, the inspection and stating what happened stay in her week. Only typing an accepted maintenance record leaves it. She gains no new decision right.
skills_to_grow: State the production count, the repair and the maintenance before a record is copied.
Leave the lift, the inspection and the choice of machine in her own hands.
role.ambitious_version: The week does not grow. She closes the same jobs, with the accepted record written for her.
